fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Entry Area; Access Drive; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Walkway; Detached Structure; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation; Fenced Sections; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear passage for emergency vehicles along the full length of the driveway.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure to keep a clear path between the main residence and detached structure for responder movement.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers or posts visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep any gates in fenced sections unlocked or install a knox box or standard responder lock to allow immediate access without delay.
• Clear a staging area near the front entry that is free of parked vehicles, equipment, or landscaping features so responders have an unobstructed work area close to the main entrance.
• Mark or identify the rear access point so responders arriving from the front can quickly locate the route to the back of the property.
• Trim shrubs and low tree branches along walkways connecting the main residence and detached structure so responders can move between structures without obstruction.
• Post the property address visibly at both the road entrance and the front entry of the main residence.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Brush Area; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation; None Visible
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Clear brush from the area where the brush concentration is visible to reduce the amount of burnable material close to the home.
• Trim lower branches from scattered trees near the structure to raise the canopy off the ground.
• Mow or cut down ground vegetation growing close to the structure and any outbuildings.
• Keep the open terrain areas free of accumulated dead grass, leaves, and debris.
• Separate any wood piles, stored materials, or outdoor furniture from shrubs and trees near the structure.
